title: Shortlist Client Profile (Data Abstraction Layer)
description: The derived, structured form of a client's raw intake (resume + intake form, spec section 2.1) -- NOT the raw upload itself. One file per client. This is the single reference point used both by the qualification gate (against job-posting.schema.json) and by the resume-tailoring engine. Modeled on JSON Resume's basics/work/skills shape, extended with tagging and gate-facing fields JSON Resume doesn't have.

client_id.description: Slug, e.g. 'jane-doe-2026'. Foreign key used by the application-tracking sheet (spec section 3) and by job-match records.

basics.description: Static header data (JSON Resume 'basics') plus target-role parameters used as gate input.

salary_floor.description: Below-floor comparison against job-posting.salary is a direct gate check.

skills.description: Full skills/experience inventory. Every entry's skill_id is the join key the gate and the tailoring engine both key off of.

last_used.description: YYYY or YYYY-MM -- lets the gate/tailoring engine down-weight stale skills.

work_history.description: JSON Resume 'work' shape, extended: bullets are individually tagged so they can be selected/recombined per application rather than locked to one resume layout (spec 2.2).

entry_id.description: Must equal the parent work_history entry's entry_id -- same field name as the parent's own key, not a new synonym. Denormalized on purpose: the tailoring engine flattens bullets across a client's whole history to score against a job's requirements, then needs this FK to re-group the selected bullets back under the right role without carrying nesting context through that pass.

text.description: The canonical, truthful, fully-composed sentence -- required and authoritative even when the structured fields below are also present.

action_verb.description: Optional decomposition, e.g. 'Facilitated'. Populate alongside task/method/metric_or_result when a bullet needs to support template-substitution rewording (see resume/tailoring-template.md §3) rather than open-ended regeneration. Not required -- decompose opportunistically during intake, text remains the fallback.

task.description: Optional decomposition, e.g. 'daily team coordination meetings'.

metric_or_result.description: Optional decomposition, e.g. '6-person engineering team, reduced sprint slippage ~15%'. Same concept as impact_metric below; kept as a separate field here because the decomposed form is consumed differently (template slot) than the standalone impact_metric (display-only callout).

items.description: skill_id, must match an entry in skills[]

skill_tags.description: Which skills this bullet demonstrates -- the tailoring engine filters/ranks bullets by overlap with a job's required + nice-to-have skill_ids. Also licenses which of the job posting's own terms may be substituted in during rewording (see resume/tailoring-template.md §3 rewording envelope: a term may only be borrowed from the posting if a skill_tag here already truthfully supports it).

theme_tags.description: Free-form themes not tied to the skill taxonomy, e.g. 'leadership', 'cost_savings'.

impact_metric.description: e.g. '$2M saved', '40% faster' -- optional, surfaced when present.

strength.description: Tailoring priority when multiple bullets compete for limited resume space.

qualification_bar.description: The client-side input to the qualification gate (spec 2.2, 2.4). Deliberately NOT a duplicate skill list -- must_have/nice_to_have reference skill_ids already defined in skills[] above, flagging which of the client's own skills are strong/core vs supplementary. The gate compares these against job-posting.requirements / nice_to_have_skills.

must_have_skill_ids.description: skill_ids the client is confident/strong in -- a job requiring these should score as a strong match.

gate_strictness.description: Operator-tunable knob for subcon_qualgate's rubric; default 'standard'.

screening_answers.description: Reusable answer bank (spec 2.2). Matched against job-posting.screening_questions[] by question_category.

question_text_template.description: Generic phrasing this answer was written for, for operator reference only.

adaptable.description: Whether the tailoring step may reword this per job, or must use it verbatim.

exclusions.description: Feeds the gate alongside skills (spec 2.2). Checked against job-posting.company / job-posting.red_flags.

consent.description: Spec 2.9 -- required before the operator applies on the client's behalf.
